```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(stagemap) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.
```

A missing arrow is easy to overlook in a flowchart, and a tracking table can fall behind the specification. `stagemap` keeps cards, links and stages in R tables, draws them as a map and checks them in code.

Attach the package with `library(stagemap)`.

## A first map

Each part of the map is a data frame: the cards, the links, the kinds of link, the stages, the steps and the changes each step makes. Pass `cards` and `stages` to `stage_map()`, pipe into `add_links()` and `add_steps()`, and print `map` to draw the live widget.

```{r first-map}
cards <- data.frame(
  id = c(
    "req_dur", "req_ae", "req_eff", "req_site",
    "spec_dur", "spec_ae", "spec_eff",
    "prog_adsl", "prog_adae", "prog_adeff",
    "test_dur", "test_ae", "test_tbl",
    "run_dur", "run_ae", "run_tbl"
  ),
  label = c(
    "Treatment duration in days", "Flag severe adverse events", "Response at week 12", "List subjects by site",
    "ADSL: TRTDURD", "ADAE: severity flag", "ADEFF: response flag",
    "adsl.R", "adae.R", "adeff.R",
    "One-day stay gives 1", "Grade 3 and above is severe", "AE table matches the listing",
    "Duration check run", "Severity check run", "Table check run"
  ),
  stage = rep(c("requirement", "specification", "program", "test", "result"), c(4, 3, 3, 3, 3)),
  lane = c(
    "Dosing", "Safety", "Efficacy", "Reporting",
    "Dosing", "Safety", "Efficacy",
    "Dosing", "Safety", "Efficacy",
    "Dosing", "Safety", "Reporting",
    "Dosing", "Safety", "Reporting"
  ),
  status = c("done", "done", "done", "waiting", rep("waiting", 12))
)
links <- data.frame(
  from = c(
    "req_dur", "req_ae", "req_eff",
    "spec_dur", "spec_ae", "spec_eff", "spec_dur", "prog_adsl",
    "prog_adsl", "prog_adae", "prog_adae", "prog_adsl",
    "test_dur", "test_ae", "test_tbl"
  ),
  to = c(
    "spec_dur", "spec_ae", "spec_eff",
    "prog_adsl", "prog_adae", "prog_adeff", "prog_adae", "prog_adeff",
    "test_dur", "test_ae", "test_tbl", "test_tbl",
    "run_dur", "run_ae", "run_tbl"
  ),
  kind = c(
    rep("specified", 3),
    rep("built", 5),
    rep("tested", 4),
    rep("result", 3)
  )
)
kinds <- data.frame(
  id = c("specified", "built", "tested", "result"),
  label = c("Specified by", "Built as", "Tested by", "Run gave"),
  line = c("solid", "dashdot", "dotted", "dashed")
)
stages <- data.frame(
  id = c("requirement", "specification", "program", "test", "result"),
  label = c("Requirement", "Specification", "Program", "Test", "Result")
)
steps <- data.frame(
  id = c("agreed", "specified", "built", "tested", "run"),
  label = c("Requirements agreed", "Specifications written", "Programs built", "Tests written", "Tests run"),
  stage = stages$id,
  text = c(
    "Four requirements are agreed with the study team.",
    "Three of them get a specification. One has none yet.",
    "Each specification becomes a program. ADAE also uses the duration rule, and ADEFF reads ADSL.",
    "Each program gets a test. One program has none.",
    "The duration check passes, the severity check fails and the table check is still running."
  )
)
changes <- data.frame(
  step = c(rep("specified", 3), rep("built", 3), rep("tested", 3), rep("run", 3)),
  card = c(
    "spec_dur", "spec_ae", "spec_eff", "prog_adsl", "prog_adae", "prog_adeff",
    "test_dur", "test_ae", "test_tbl", "run_dur", "run_ae", "run_tbl"
  ),
  status = c(rep("done", 9), "done", "failed", "running")
)
map <- stage_map(cards, stages, title = "Analysis traceability") |>
  add_links(links, kinds = kinds) |>
  add_steps(steps, changes = changes, intro = "Follow one analysis from requirement to result.")
map
```

## What you see

Columns show stages from left to right, and rows group cards into lanes. Arrows follow the `links` table, and the legend above the grid matches each line style to its kind label. Hover over a card, or tap it, to read its stage, lane and status in the panel below the map. A click picks the card; a second click lets go. In Shiny the pick reaches the server (see "Stage maps in Shiny" below).

The player at the top right plays the steps: Play, Back, Next and Reset, and a list of the steps below. Each step changes the statuses of some cards, so the map shows the analysis as it moved from requirement to result.

## Why stagemap exists

A week before a review, a programmer is asked which study requirements have no test. When the links live in a slide and a spreadsheet, the answer means cross-checking by hand. With cards and links in R, the map and the checks read the same tables, so the answer is a function call and a highlighted card. The map and the checks help reviewers inspect links; qualification of the software stays with your own procedures.

## Ask the map questions

Three functions inspect the same `map` widget and return plain data frames. `sm_trace()` walks links from a starting card, `sm_orphans()` finds cards with no links at all, and `sm_missing()` lists cards in one stage with no direct link to another stage.

```{r ask-map}
ae_trace <- sm_trace(map, "req_ae")
ae_trace

sm_orphans(map)

sm_missing(map, "requirement", linked_to = "specification")

sm_missing(map, "program", linked_to = "test")
```

Pass the traced card identifiers to `stage_map_highlight()` to keep that path clear and fade the rest on the first draw.

```{r highlight-trace}
stage_map_highlight(map, ae_trace$id)
```

## Kinds of link and statuses

`add_links()` accepts a `kinds` data frame with `id`, `label`, `line` (`"solid"`, `"dashed"`, `"dotted"`, or `"dashdot"`), `end` (`"arrow"`, `"ring"`, or `"none"`), `tone`, and `quiet`. Leaving `kinds = NULL` draws every link as a plain arrow.

Cards take one of five built-in `status` values: `"done"`, `"running"`, `"waiting"`, `"failed"`, and `"skipped"`. Pass `statuses` to `stage_map()` as a named character vector such as `c(done = "Pass", failed = "Not passed")` to relabel built-in statuses, or as a data frame with `id`, `label`, `tone`, and `icon` to restyle them or add your own.

## Zones and steps

`add_zones()` draws a labelled outline around cards that share a `zone` column value. `add_steps()`, used in the first map, takes `steps` (one row per step, with an optional caption in `text`) and `changes`, which lists the cards whose status, stage or visibility change at a step. A card given a new `stage` glides there.

```{r zones}
cards_review <- cards
cards_review$zone <- ifelse(cards_review$lane == "Safety", "qc", NA)

stage_map(cards_review, stages, title = "Safety review") |>
  add_links(links, kinds = kinds) |>
  add_zones(data.frame(
    id = "qc",
    label = "Safety review",
    note = "Re-run after updating the severity rule."
  ))
```

## Stage maps in Shiny

Put `stage_map_output()` in the UI and `render_stage_map()` in the server. Read the reader's selection from `input$map_selected`, and update the drawn map without redrawing it through `stage_map_proxy()`.

```{r shiny-app, eval = FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(stagemap)

cards <- data.frame(
  id = c("req_ae", "spec_ae", "test_ae"),
  label = c("Flag severe adverse events", "ADAE: severity flag", "Grade 3 and above is severe"),
  stage = c("requirement", "specification", "test"),
  lane = "Safety"
)
links <- data.frame(from = c("req_ae", "spec_ae"), to = c("spec_ae", "test_ae"))
map <- stage_map(cards, title = "Safety check") |> add_links(links)

ui <- fluidPage(
  stage_map_output("map"),
  actionButton("trace_ae", "Highlight AE trace"),
  verbatimTextOutput("selected")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$map <- render_stage_map(map)
  output$selected <- renderPrint(input$map_selected)

  observeEvent(input$trace_ae, {
    ids <- sm_trace(map, "req_ae")$id
    stage_map_proxy("map") |> stage_map_highlight(ids)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Run the bundled demo app with `shiny::runApp(system.file("examples", "shiny-demo", package = "stagemap"))`.
